messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Dropping/keeping levels in scales
parts:
Hi, a recent discussion in R-help has made me aware that the options
for dropping or keeping the levels in the scales of plots are not
correctly implemented in the Plot Builder. This is partly due to
misleading indications in the ggplot2 web documentation.

If, for instance, you use ggplot2 to produce a bar chart from a factor
that has zero counts in some level, by default that level is dropped
in the plot. You can override this default behaviour with
scale_x_discrete(drop=FALSE). See an example discussed here:
https://mailman.stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2012-March/306853.html

The default value of this "drop" parameter is TRUE, as seen in
?discrete_scale
However, in the web documentation says that it is FALSE!

Perhaps for that reason the Plot Builder dialog has an unchecked
checkbox for "Drop unused levels" in the element
"scale_x_discrete" (and "scale_y_discrete"). If you check that box,
the parameter drop=TRUE is added, but this is just the same as doing
nothing. The result is that you cannot change the behaviour of that
parameter. (A workaround is telling explicit limits to add the levels
with zero counts.)

I don't know what should be done.The current dialog is coherent with
the web documentation of ggplot2, but it doesn't work as expected!

Helios

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Dropping/keeping levels in scales
parts:
You are right, I think that this may have been an undocumented change
in ggplot2 version 0.9.0. I've fixed it in dev.

Ian

messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Re: Dropping/keeping levels in scales
parts:
Thanks, Ian. You are doing a wonderful work.
You are right as well: I have tested previous versions of ggplot2 and
Deducer, and the option worked as expected.
I have found another, related issue:

The tab "Options" for stat_bin also has a checkbox for "drop". It is
checked by default, and if you uncheck it the parameter drop=FALSE is
added to stat_bin(). However, there are two problems with this:

1. According to the documentation, the default value of this parameter
is already FALSE, so we are in a similar situation as with the scales.

2. If the element you are modifying is not a "stat_bin" layer, but a
"geom" like "geom_bar" or "geom_histogram", that uses "bin" as "stat",
the parameter "drop=FALSE" is added to geom_bar(), geom_histogram(),
etc., instead to stat_bin() -- I hope this sentence is not just a
tongue-twister. But that parameter is not recognized by those geoms.

However, even if that is fixed in Deducer, the bad news is that
ggplot2 won't work as expected. It seems that the parameter "drop" in
stat_bin() does not work, as reported by Ben Bolker in R-help. So
perhaps it's not worth to change that part of the Plot Builder, until
ggplot2 fixes that.

Helios
